notes.TWN: Governed by the Republic of China (Taipei); claimed by the People’s Republic of China. Its status is disputed, so it is drawn neither as a sovereign state nor as a province of China.
notes.KOS: Declared independence from Serbia in 2008; recognised by about half of UN members, not by Serbia.
notes.SOL: Self-governing since 1991; internationally regarded as part of Somalia.
notes.CYN: Recognised only by Turkey; internationally regarded as part of Cyprus.
notes.SAH: Non-self-governing territory (UN list); mostly administered by Morocco, claimed by the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic.
notes.FLK: British Overseas Territory; claimed by Argentina as the Islas Malvinas.
notes.PRI: Unincorporated territory of the United States; residents are US citizens.
notes.HKG: Special Administrative Region of China; separate statistics.
notes.MAC: Special Administrative Region of China; separate statistics.
notes.GUF: Overseas department and region of France (part of the EU).
notes.GLP: Overseas department and region of France (part of the EU).
notes.MTQ: Overseas department and region of France (part of the EU).
notes.REU: Overseas department and region of France (part of the EU).
notes.MYT: Overseas department and region of France (part of the EU).
notes.BES: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba: special municipalities of the Netherlands.
notes.NIR: Part of the United Kingdom; under the 1998 Good Friday Agreement it may join Ireland if a majority votes for it.
notes.UAOCC: Internationally recognised as part of Ukraine; annexed and administered by Russia since 2014. Crimea’s value is from Russia’s 2014 census of the peninsula: Crimean Tatars, Tatars and Azerbaijanis as a share of residents who stated a nationality.
notes.OCC: Under Russian military occupation (Crimea and parts of Donetsk and Luhansk since 2014, more since 2022); internationally recognised as part of Ukraine. Line of control: DeepState map, 17 Oct 2026.
notes.KRI: Kurdistan Region — the autonomous region of Iraq (Erbil, Duhok, Sulaymaniyah, Halabja). No separate religion figures; the value shown is Iraq’s national estimate.
